newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp bonds shrug off stock market surge.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp bonds shrug off stock market surge.

text.p: A dramatic surge in the U.S. stock market on the Wednesday following election day, had little impact on the U.S. corporate bond markets, which remained little changed, traders said.

"The corporate bond market did not participate in the stock market's upside," said one high-yield trader. "If the Treasury market had rallied, we would have taken off. This was a day just for stock jockeys."
The price on the benchmark 30-year Treasury dropped 13/32 to 101-23/32, to yield 6.62 percent.

Primary market activity in corporate bonds was slower today as well, syndicate officials said. Toll Brothers Corp, a homebuilding company, made use of the lull by selling $100 million in 8.75 percent senior subordinate notes through Salomon Brothers via a public shelf offering. Pillowtex Corp, a maker of blankets and pillows, sold $125 million of 10 percent senior subordinate notes due 2006 in a 144 private placement via NationsBanc Capital Markets Inc.
Sources familiar with the offering said it was six times oversubscribed. They noted the bonds traded at a 101 bid soon after the deal was priced, signifying continued strong demand.
While several investment-grade issuers like El Paso Natural Gas Co were rumoured to be close to hitting the market this Wednesday, no deals materialized.
Syndicate officials speculated the delay may continue throughout the week.

"We still have a Treasury refunding on Thursday, an early close (of the Treasury market) on Friday, and Monday is a holiday. There's a possibility potential issuers will just wait for next week," said one syndicate source.
With prices in the broader market unchanged, secondary market activity centered on bonds with special situations.

Flagstar Corp senior and suborindate debt closed the day up one point after the company stated in a conference call with investors that it was closer to reaching a restructing on its burdgeoning outstanding debt load.

Trump's Castle bonds traded down 2 1/2 to three points and Trump Atlantic City Funding bonds traded down one point as a result of negative views among investors about the company's ongoing negotiations with the Rank Organization Plc, traders said.
